title: The Clockwork Seagull
author: Barış Kısır
premise: When the clockwork seagull built by twelve-year-old Linus inherits its inventor's final message, Linus and his brass bird must cross the steam-filled city of Meridian to deliver a stolen gear — a gear that, if it reaches the Clocktower, will stop the city's eternal fog and reveal what the Council has been hiding in the mist.
short_description: Twelve-year-old Linus and his clockwork seagull must deliver a stolen gear to the Clocktower — a gear that will lift the fog and reveal what the Council hides in the mist.
long_description: In Meridian, a brass-and-cobble city where the fog is engineered and the steam never stops, twelve-year-old Linus Okafor finishes the clockwork seagull his grandfather left half-built — and the gull's head holds a recording: "Take the gear to the Clocktower. It stops the fog. Trust no uniform." With Wren, a messenger girl who knows every rooftop, Kettle, a retired boiler-car driver, and a rescued under-city girl named Minnow, Linus crosses the steam districts, the water-lock quarter, and the market of gears — chased by the Fog-Master's clockwork hawks — to place the gear in the great clock's heart and lift the fog from a secret the Council has sealed beneath the steam: a drowned under-city, full of people.
main_characters: Linus Okafor — twelve, inventive, shy, brave
The Seagull — brassy, moody, loyal; speaks in chimes and scratches
Wren — messenger girl, fast, funny, secretly kind
Kettle — retired boiler-car driver, gruff, warm, steam-bearded
Grandfather Amos — dead but present via notes and the gull
Fog-Master Hale — cold, methodical, afraid of the light
Minnow — a small rescued under-city girl
